legend.text:
Ten views of one system. Colour means the same thing on every page; position means
ownership; an arrow is reserved for the relationships position cannot express.
three conventions, and that is the whole vocabulary
solid carries traffic or creates; dashed only references
generated from the repos, not drawn by hand
no arrow needed to say so
the two or three that matter
solid — A creates or calls B
not from a doc that drifted
Why ten views and not one

No single diagram of this system
is both complete and readable.
Each page answers one question and
drops everything irrelevant to it,
which is why the same component
appears on several pages wearing
different detail.
A dashed box is a boundary
Inside it means owned by it
A filled box is the point

org.text:
Every repo plays one of three roles: what the factory consumes, what it produces, or the
factory itself. The deploy substrate sits between them.
the vocabulary the factory designs against
slow-moving cloud + cluster layers — shared by every tenant
standalone repos, each a Helm chart + a Platform CR

substrate.text:
landing-zone, by layer. Organization components run once in the management account;
everything below them is per-environment.
one VPC per environment — owned or adopted
a tenant's stores are a declaration, not a component

Adding a tenant edits a map. Its
databases, buckets, queues and
caches are written on
Platform.spec.datastores and
provisioned by the generic
tenant-substrate module — there is
no per-app component to write.

network.text:
One component, two modes. In create mode it owns a VPC; in adopt mode it builds nothing and
re-exports someone else's through the same outputs.
management account — the address space and the backbone
the single-account default — this component owns the VPC
network-owner account — the far side of adopt
one hub per transit gateway — every environment shares its NAT IPs
The cluster that lands on it
wires against one output contract either way
fails at plan, not at apply

addons.text:
One ApplicationSet per group, ordered by sync wave. A cluster opts in with a label; the
generators do the rest.
nothing else can reconcile until these are up
nodes, then the rules that govern them
the OTLP waist and its backends
workflow engine, then the dashboards that read it

otel-gateway and
otel-gateway-floor answer on the
same telemetry.monitoring alias,
and their ApplicationSets select
mutually exclusive tiers. A tenant
chart is byte-identical across
them.

A cluster opts in with one label
and the generators do the rest.
Ordering lives in the sync-wave
annotation, so ArgoCD enforces it
rather than anyone remembering an
install order.

control-plane.text:
One binary, nine reconcilers, one leader-election lease. Each zone below is a reconciler;
what sits inside it is what that reconciler creates and keeps true.
three capability groups under nanohype.dev — the whole public API
the three loops that can stop a tenant
resolved at the top of every workload reconcile

Nine reconcilers share a single
leader-election lease. Splitting
them is trivial if one outgrows
the rest; running six deployments
before that happens is just more
to operate.

Fast state here, slow state in
OpenTofu

Per-tenant IAM, KMS grants and
model access reconcile through the
AWS SDK because a Platform apply
must not wait on a Terragrunt run.
Buckets, keys, endpoints and the
event bus stay in landing-zone.

request-path.text:
One invocation, app to model and back. The app holds no AWS credential and signs nothing —
the gateway does, as the tenant.
inference leaves the cluster; nothing else does
the record the agent's account gets checked against
run as the tenant, not a server

Steps 2 and 3 are where this
breaks

extproc registers a body-parsing
processor per endpoint path. A
request to an unregistered prefix
never has its model read out of
the body, never gets
x-ai-eg-model, and matches no
route — so every call fails while
the Gateway still reports healthy.

It holds no AWS credential. Envoy
signs SigV4 as the tenant
ServiceAccount, so the audit
record and the agent's own account
of what it did name the same
principal.

identity.text:
Isolation is a spectrum, not a boolean. Two orthogonal dials — where the control-plane CRs
live, and how hard the workload boundary is.
no role ARN is ever pasted into a chart
every Resource scoped by naming convention or exact ARN
a breach of the auditor role surfaces history, not content
growing up a tier is a value change, never a migration
the boundary the tenant cannot reach around
guardrails no workload role can escape

observability.text:
One neutral waist. Producers emit OTLP to a stable alias; which backends exist behind it is
a property of the cluster tier.
telemetry.monitoring.svc:4317 — the same name in every tier
the tier is which of these exist
burn rate is not just an alert here

governance.text:
Budget, SLO, and eval each close a loop that can stop a tenant. Recovery from the budget one
is exclusively human.
AWS-side only — it cannot reach the cluster
no CR mutation, no API path back

lifecycle.text:
Two vending lines, one layer apart. Both write manifests to git; the cluster always wins on
read.
a form, a CR, or a factory run
the source of truth for what should exist
ArgoCD applies; the operator reconciles what lands
